extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies, agency rulemakers, administrative law practitioners, and the bar
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for federal administrative procedure generally, with specific treatment of hearing procedures (hearing examiners), rules on depositions, official notice, admission and discipline of attorneys, prehearing conferences, and statistical metrics for assessing hearing performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of the Office of Administrative Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: With a view to achieving improvements in administrative procedures within the Executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government, the Office shall: (a) carry on continuous studies of the adequacy of the procedures by which Federal departments and agencies determine the rights, duties, and privileges of persons; (b) initiate cooperative effort among the departments and agencies and their respective bars to develop and adopt so far as practicable uniform rules of practice and procedure; (c) collect and publish facts and statistics concerning the procedures of the departments and agencies; (d) assist departments and agencies in the formulation and improvement of their administrative procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office acts in an advisory capacity; it secures cooperation and advice of departments/agencies and the bar; it issues annual reports and special reports at the Attorney General's request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for reviewing procedural legislation and proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining procedural provisions of proposed legislation or agency proposals, inquiry is made whether the proposed procedures are lawful in the constitutional sense, whether they conform to the pattern of the Administrative Procedure Act, and whether they are uniform with other procedures in the same field and related fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further inquiry: whether procedures are fair to all concerned (Government, public, regulated parties); whether procedures are reasonable and uniform (to the extent practicable); whether they are clear and simple; and whether they are designed to accomplish the regulatory purpose with economy and dispatch. If substantial defects are found, the Office may seek informal conference with agency staff and suggest revisions; agencies are not required to accept views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition/admission of attorneys to practice before agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed uniform rule: any person who is a member in good standing of the bar of the Supreme Court of the United States or of the highest court of any State, Territory, or of the District of Columbia, and who is not under any order of any court restricting him in the practice of law, may represent others before the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text of proposed rule circulated to agencies; several agencies adopted language in substance. 'Signature to constitute certificate': personal appearance or signature constitutes representation to the agency that the person is authorized and qualified to represent the party; further proof may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on and recognition of attorneys (service-of-process rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: When any participant in any matter before an agency is represented by an attorney and that fact has been made known in writing to the agency, any notice or other written communication required or permitted to be given to or by such participant shall be given to or by such attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where statute specifically provides another method of service, that method also must be used; if a participant is represented by more than one attorney, service upon any one of them is sufficient. Proposed rule embodies substance of prevailing agency practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline and disbarment of attorneys before agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should have simple, adequate, and uniform rules for discipline of attorneys guilty of misconduct or who fall short of high standards of professional integrity. Existing agency rules vary; grounds include 'good cause', 'unfit' conduct, violations of conduct rules, and misconduct at hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables summarize which agencies permit summary suspension, grounds for disbarment, prerequisites, notice to be given, whether hearing is afforded, and whether disbarment by other courts or administrative agencies is recognized. The Office has under study measures to improve and make uniform agency rules for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: General hearing-procedures quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous study of agency procedures for the conduct of administrative hearings focusing on adequacy, efficiency, and uniformity of procedures used throughout the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes study and recommendations for agency codes (major and minor rulemaking studies), and specific procedural areas such as official notice, service of process, subpoenas, depositions and interrogatories, and the use of prehearing conference techniques. Charts and illustrative rules are published to promote uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notice — matters appropriate for official notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 1 (Matters of Law): the Agency or its hearing officer may officially notice federal law (Constitution, Acts, decisions, Executive Orders, Federal Register), state law (public laws and decisions of state courts), governmental organization (officers, departments), and agency organization (organization, administration, official publications, practitioners). Rule 2 (Material Facts): in absence of controverting evidence, may officially notice agency proceedings (pendency, issues, dispositions), general business customs, notorious facts (widely known facts) and technical knowledge within the agency's expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for taking official notice: any party may request or the hearing officer/agency may suggest official notice; if a decision rests on official notice it must state the fact clearly; any party may controvert notice at the time it is made (or by appropriate exceptions/reconsideration if prior opportunity was lacking). The officer may consult any source whether or not furnished by parties or admissible under rules of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conferences — initiation and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Prehearing conferences may be initiated by agency rules or the presiding officer for purposes such as formulating issues, simplifying the case, considering admissions, stipulations, scheduling, and other objectives of case management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where circumstances make a conference impracticable, presiding officer may request correspondence to accomplish similar objectives; some agencies omit conferences in certain proceedings (e.g., economic enforcement where issues are drawn by pleadings); illustrative agency rules and footnotes describe permissible substitutions (written submissions in lieu of personal appearance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions — oral depositions and depositions upon interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed procedural rules for depositions: service of notice; production of books, papers, documents and tangible things; officer before whom deposition is taken must administer oath, record testimony (stenographic or transcription), note objections on the deposition, permit signing/attestation and return, and forward the deposition to the Agency Secretary; depositions upon interrogatories include timelines for cross- and redirect-interrogatories (10 days for cross after notice, 5 days for redirect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination may be via transmission of written cross-interrogatories to the officer who propounds them seriatim after direct testimony; officer certifies and files deposition, parties are notified; depositions are not part of the record until received in evidence by the hearing officer, and ordinarily received only in entirety; fees for officers and deponents follow District Court schedules and are paid by the party taking the deposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened procedures (decisions without evidentiary hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures permitting examiners to issue decisions on the merits without evidentiary hearings (e.g., decisions based upon written submissions), used to dispose of certain types of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical findings: of proceedings disposed by examiners in FY1957, 69.4% were decided after evidentiary hearings and 9.4% by decisions on the merits without evidentiary hearings. Use varies by agency and proceeding type (e.g., ICC shortened-procedure cases decided faster; CAB 'shortened' cases were commonly 'non-hearing' cases used for convenience and cost savings rather than time savings). Comparative time-to-disposition data and caveats for interpretation are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing-examiner statistical/performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard metrics collected and published for proceedings before hearing examiners: backlog and volume (cases pending at start and end of period), new cases assigned, old cases remanded, cases disposed by examiners, manner of disposition, age of proceedings (measured from assignment to examiner), use of shortened procedures, time intervals for stages of proceedings (assignment to decision, assignment to opening of hearing, length of hearings, time from close to submission, submission to issuance), number of hearings reopened, suspensions on interlocutory appeals, and prehearing conferences held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional staffing metrics: number of examiners employed, borrowed/loaned examiners, computed man-years, average number of days spent in hearings/prehearing conferences per man-year, average number of decisions on the merits per man-year, and number of proceedings assigned for hearing only (record certification). Tables and sampling methods (e.g., extensions where full-year data unavailable) and caveats about cross-agency comparisons are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency rules on subpoenas, production and discovery practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies maintain varying rules governing subpoenas, production of documents, depositions, and interrogatories; these rules are charted and compared with illustrative rules of the President's Conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office prepared charts identifying salient features of present agency rules on subpoenas and depositions to aid efforts to develop uniform and adequate rules; examples include procedural limits, service, checking admissibility and motions to suppress depositions or parts thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for admission and agency-specific admission practices
rubrics_metrics.description: As of Dec 31, 1957, ten agencies still had rules for formal admission of attorneys (application, certificate of court, examination). The Office recommended dispensing with formal admission procedures in favor of the proposed uniform rule admitting attorneys in good standing of highest state/federal courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report includes a table listing which agencies required application, certificate of court admission, or examination, and notes recent adoptions and declinations by agencies (e.g., several agencies adopted the proposal; Patent Office declined).
